title: Einstein's 1923 paper saying general relativity fits with the ether

tellings.quote: there's even actually a paper I think in 1923 where Einstein says general relativity is in fact compatible with The Ether

tellings.difference: Dates the paper to 1921, not 1923, and is told by Salvatore Pais.
tellings.link_reason: Both are about Einstein's early-1920s paper bringing back the ether as compatible with general relativity.

tellings.page: Ether and the Theory of Relativity
tellings.quote: Recapitulating, we may say that according to the general theory of relativity space is endowed with physical qualities; in this sense, therefore, there exists an ether.

tellings.page: Ether and the Theory of Relativity
tellings.quote: According to the general theory of relativity space without ether is unthinkable; for in such space there not only would be no propagation of light, but also no possibility of existence for standards of space and time (measuring-rods and clocks), nor therefore any space-time intervals in the physical sense.

tellings.page: Ether and the Theory of Relativity
tellings.quote: But this ether may not be thought of as endowed with the quality characteristic of ponderable media, as consisting of parts which may be tracked through time. The idea of motion may not be applied to it.

tellings.page: Ether and the Theory of Relativity
tellings.quote: More careful reflection teaches us, however, that the special theory of relativity does not compel us to deny ether.

plain: The claim is that the physicist Albert Einstein, whose theory of relativity is usually thought to have done away with the 'ether' (an old idea of an invisible medium filling all of space), later wrote that his general theory of relativity fits with an ether after all. Michels raises it himself, recalling 'a paper I think in 1923.' The Navy scientist Salvatore Pais, known for unusual patents, says that although Einstein was set against the idea, he brought it back in a paper in 1921. The work they mean is Einstein's 'Ether and the Theory of Relativity,' an address he gave at the University of Leiden on May 5, 1920, so it dates from 1920, not 1923 as Michels says or 1921 as Pais says. In it Einstein says that 'according to the general theory of relativity space is endowed with physical qualities; in this sense, therefore, there exists an ether,' and that 'space without ether is unthinkable.' He also says this ether may not be thought of as made of parts that can be tracked through time, and that 'The idea of motion may not be applied to it.' If the tellers are right, the founder of modern relativity left room for a physical medium in empty space, an idea some see as opening the door to new physics.

discussion.by: Ether and the Theory of Relativity
discussion.text: The text in Einstein's Sidelights on Relativity reads "An Address delivered on May 5th, 1920, in the University of Leyden", so the work the tellers mean dates from 1920, where the host says 1923 and Salvatore Pais 1921. In it Einstein says that "according to the general theory of relativity space is endowed with physical qualities; in this sense, therefore, there exists an ether", the claim the tellers give it.
